params.body:
Closes #1130

Replaces #1131 and #1133 (the gateway cannot add a commit to an existing branch). #1131 failed on the format of the new test; #1133 was built on the `main` before #1132 (Symfony 8.1.12), so the audit and up-to-date jobs failed. This one is built on the current `main`, the test formatted with Pint.

## What was wrong

A vehicle's first photos are re-sorted by file name after the upload (R S1-6.3): once when the uploader is done (`ImageController::reset_image_order`) and again when the sheet opens on photos that start at 0 (`OwnStockController::create`). Both used MySQL `ORDER BY name`, which compares character by character. A garage that uploads `1.jpg` to `14.jpg` sees them 1, 2 ... 14 in its folder, and got 1, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 2 ... 9 on the photo tab: the first places shuffled, the rest in order. That is the pattern reported in Portal mail:69.

## What changes

- `App\Support\PhotoUploadOrder::byFileName()` is the one rule for both places: file names compared the way Windows Explorer and the macOS Finder show them (`strnatcasecmp`: numbers by value, case ignored), upload order (id) on a tie. A row without a name sorts first, as it did with MySQL.
- `reset_image_order` and the re-sort in `create` use it; the rest of both stays as it was (steps of one from 0 with the first as main photo, steps of ten on the sheet).
- The sort by name stays. It makes the order independent of how a file dialog or a drag hands the files over.
- R S1-6.3 says how names compare and what happened before. The phpstan baseline drops one `$photo` access in `ImageController`.

Uploads to a vehicle that already has photos are not affected: those keep the order they were sent in (`max(sort_order) + 1`, one file at a time).

## Tests

`FirstPhotosFollowTheFolderOrderTest`: fourteen numbered files after the uploader's reset, twelve after opening the sheet (steps of ten), mixed-case and camera names, a tie on the same name, and another garage refused. The two flow tests fail on `main` and pass here. Full suite 3337 green on the current `main`, `composer audit` clean, phpstan clean.

The file names of the reported vehicle were not read (no production access from the workbench); the numbered-name case is the one that produces this exact pattern.
params.title: The first photos of a vehicle stand in the order its folder shows them
